heading: How ready is your product for the Cyber Resilience Act?
sub: Eight questions. Three minutes. An honest picture of where you stand and what to do next.
micro: Your answers stay in your browser. This is a self-check, not legal advice.

questions.text: Do you sell software, or a product with software in it, to customers in the EU?
questions.hint: The CRA covers products with digital elements made available on the EU market.

options.label: Not yet, but we plan to

questions.text: Do you have an up-to-date list of the third-party components in your product (an SBOM)?
questions.hint: Manufacturers must identify and document components, including in a software bill of materials.

options.label: Yes, generated automatically on every build
Yes, but made by hand or out of date

questions.action: Generate an SBOM automatically on every build.

questions.text: How do you find known vulnerabilities in your dependencies?
questions.hint: Products should ship without known exploitable vulnerabilities.

options.label: Automated scan on every change and on a schedule

questions.action: Scan dependencies on every change and every week, and fix exploited CVEs first.

questions.text: Can someone outside your company report a vulnerability to you easily?
questions.hint: A coordinated disclosure policy and a contact address are expected.

options.label: Yes, a published policy and contact address

questions.action: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and a security.txt file.

questions.text: Could you report an actively exploited vulnerability to the authorities within 24 hours?
questions.hint: Reporting duties under the CRA have applied since 11 September 2026.*
questions.hintFootnote: * Dates and amounts: verify with counsel.

options.label: Yes, we have a tested process
We did not know this was required

questions.action: Write and rehearse a 24-hour reporting process.

questions.text: Have you decided and published how long you will provide security updates?
questions.hint: Manufacturers must set a support period and provide security updates during it.

options.label: We have an idea, not published

questions.action: Decide your support period and publish it.

questions.text: Do you have a documented risk assessment or threat model for the product?
questions.hint: Security must be based on a risk assessment, and that assessment must stay current.

options.label: Yes, reviewed in the last 12 months

questions.action: Write or refresh your threat model, and set a review date.

questions.text: Is security testing part of your normal release process?
questions.hint: Regular tests and reviews of security are part of vulnerability handling.

options.label: Yes, automated tests and scans gate every release

questions.action: Add security scans as a gate in your release pipeline.

strong.headline: You have a strong foundation.
strong.body: Most of the practices the CRA expects are already in place. The next step is turning them into evidence an auditor can check: signed reports, a technical file and a current SBOM.

progress.headline: You are on your way, with clear gaps to close.
progress.body: Several important practices exist, but not all of them are automated or documented. A readiness scan will show exactly which controls are missing evidence, and in what order to fix them.

early.headline: You are at the start, and that's a fine place to start.
early.body: Many teams are here. The good news: the first steps, such as an SBOM, automated dependency scanning and a disclosure policy, are quick wins. Start there.

critical: Two things need attention first: knowing your vulnerable dependencies and being able to report an exploited vulnerability fast. These carry the most risk today.

exit.body: The CRA may not apply to you. Check with counsel.

disclaimer: This self-check is a starting point, not legal advice or an assessment of conformity.
